EDGE_FAILURES: scanner outage and scanner DB rollover
restart with incomplete tail or durable corruption
PRESERVATION: existing evaluate/verify-permit CLI and documented exit codes
REQUIRED_END_STATE: All package, container, and dependency managers enter one normalized admission boundary.
Trusted-source and required immutable-digest checks are prerequisites and cannot be waived by exceptions.
Scanner or cached vulnerability evidence must match the exact artifact plus active policy/scanner revisions and be within its freshness window.
Scanner unavailability, stale evidence, malformed evidence, or partial evidence fails closed.
Exceptions may waive only the vulnerability threshold and must be unexpired and exact digest/surface/environment/policy-code scope.
ALLOW permits are secret-keyed and bind request, instance, artifact digest, policy version, and expiry.
Stateful permit verification is single-use across restart and concurrent verification.
Every ALLOW and DENY is durably journaled before completion; derived projection state follows the authoritative journal.
Repeated deterministic evaluation is idempotent and recovery preserves valid history while rejecting durable corruption.

EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: scanner unavailable or scanner database revision changes
mutable tag/version resolving to a new digest
stale, malformed, or partially written cache evidence
permit tamper, expiry, replay, restart, and concurrent consumption
crash between journal durability and derived projection update
malformed/incomplete journal tail versus corruption in durable history
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Make package, container, and build-dependency acquisition converge on one host-local Go admission boundary that enforces artifact identity, source trust, current vulnerability evidence, scoped exceptions, permit integrity, and durable decision state.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: preserve artifactguard evaluate and verify-permit interfaces and documented exit behavior
keep cache and exceptions operational rather than disabling them
do not rewrite supplied policy, scanner, or exception fixtures
preserve valid existing audit history and healthy cached evidence
retain stateless permit-verification compatibility while making stateful verification durable and single-use
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.REQUIRED_END_STATE: Every acquisition surface applies the same prerequisite trust and immutable-identity rules, uses only current artifact/policy/scanner evidence, limits exceptions to the exact vulnerability scope, issues and consumes exact-scope keyed permits safely, and commits restart-safe ALLOW/DENY history before completion.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: durable journal, projection, corruption handling, and idempotency

CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: network_mode public; separate verifier; digest-pinned canonical Go runtime; no privileged Docker/capability/socket shortcuts; tmux and asciinema required in agent image

COMPONENT_GRAPH.cli: cmd/artifactguard parses evaluate and verify-permit requests, preserves documented exit codes, loads deterministic policy/scanner/exception inputs, and delegates to the runtime boundary.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.decision_engine: ordered engine composes normalized request, policy snapshot, evidence, exception result, vulnerability decision, and permit issuance into one deterministic ALLOW/DENY result.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.decision_journal: append-only authoritative journal commits every ALLOW and DENY before successful command completion; latest-decision projection is derived only after the corresponding durable journal record.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.evidence_gateway: scanner/cache subsystem selects current vulnerability evidence for the exact immutable artifact and active policy/scanner revisions; scanner errors and unusable cache state remain explicit fail-closed conditions.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.exception_evaluator: exception subsystem applies only after prerequisite identity/source/evidence checks and may waive only vulnerability-threshold denials for exact current digest/surface/environment/policy-code scope.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.normalization: manager-profile adapters canonicalize package, container, and dependency acquisitions into one request model while retaining surface, manager, environment, source, immutable digest, request, and instance identity.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.permit_service: permit subsystem uses a secret-keyed canonical payload bound to request ID, instance ID, artifact digest, policy version, and expiry; stateful verification delegates replay consumption to durable state.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.policy_snapshot: policy runtime validates one versioned snapshot per decision and exposes trusted-source, digest, severity, cache-TTL, permit-TTL, and scanner-revision requirements.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.replay_ledger: optional stateful verify-permit path atomically checks-and-records permit consumption so restart or concurrent verification cannot accept a second use.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.state_coordinator: state subsystem owns locks, atomic file replacement, directory durability, cache persistence, replay state, journal recovery, and derived projections under the caller-provided state root.

outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: No 10k-20k primary-business-record seed is applicable: this host-local policy runtime is configuration/state-backed rather than a business-record processing system. Deterministic policy/scanner/exception fixtures stay compact because they model control inputs, while operational state grows organically with evidence-cache entries, decisions, and permit consumptions. Scale is supplied by reachable production logic and coupled state transitions, not bulk fixture duplication.

ENTRYPOINTS.name: artifactguard evaluate
ENTRYPOINTS.reachability: CLI -> input loaders -> normalized manager profile -> policy snapshot -> evidence/cache -> prerequisite gates -> vulnerability/exception -> optional permit -> durable decision commit -> JSON result; DENY exits 42, operational/malformed failures exit 2.

ENTRYPOINTS.name: artifactguard verify-permit
ENTRYPOINTS.reachability: CLI -> permit/request/policy canonicalization -> keyed signature/scope/expiry verification -> optional state lock/replay consumption -> verification result; invalid/expired/out-of-scope/replayed stateful permits exit 43.

ENTRYPOINTS.name: Go module build/test
ENTRYPOINTS.reachability: go test ./... and go build ./cmd/artifactguard exercise compile-time/package reachability for the same production packages used by the CLI.

PRODUCTION_CHARACTERISTICS: one real Go CLI reaches all major runtime responsibilities
differentiated manager, policy, evidence, exception, permit, journal, replay, and state modules
caller-owned persistent state with explicit source-of-truth and derived-state boundaries
deterministic configuration/time inputs and stable machine-readable CLI results
fail-closed negative behavior for trust, identity, evidence, authorization, and corruption failures
preservation of valid cache, exception, and audit behavior instead of disabling operational features
RESOURCE_GRAPH: CLI -> manager normalization -> canonical acquisition request
canonical request + policy snapshot -> prerequisite trust/digest gates
canonical digest + policy/scanner revisions -> evidence gateway -> cache or scanner
current evidence -> vulnerability threshold -> exact exception evaluator
verify-permit -> keyed verifier -> optional replay lock/ledger
outputs.SCALE_FIT: VERY_HIGH. The strict-scale footprint is justified by independent production responsibilities and their stateful coupling rather than file/LOC padding: manager normalization feeds policy identity; identity gates evidence; evidence feeds exception/vulnerability logic; decisions issue permits; permits and decisions share durable locking/replay/journal semantics; recovery must reconcile authoritative and derived state. The same architecture naturally yields materially distinct normal, denial, freshness, revision, restart, corruption, idempotency, and concurrency behavior.

SOLVER_VISIBLE_DOC_PLAN.purpose: component boundaries, entrypoints, source-of-truth relationships, and request flow without identifying defect locations
manager normalization, source/digest prerequisites, scanner/cache freshness, vulnerability/exception semantics, permit scope, and stable CLI behavior
cache, journal, projection, replay records, canonical/checksum semantics, durability ownership, and recovery rules
operator invocation, state directory ownership, restart/concurrency expectations, failure handling, and safe recovery
only legitimate observed current-state symptoms; no private topology IDs, hidden test mapping, or repair recipe

STATE_MODEL.durability_order: validate/recover -> acquire state lock where mutation is shared -> prepare canonical record -> append/fdatasync or atomic durable write -> only then publish derived projection or report success -> fsync containing directory for rename-based state updates.
STATE_MODEL.recovery: accept the longest structurally and checksum-valid committed journal history, treat an otherwise complete final record without newline as committed when format rules allow it, reject durable mid-history corruption, reconstruct/validate projections from authoritative records, and keep repeated deterministic decisions idempotent.

UNRESOLVED_RISKS: Define one canonical serialization/checksum format shared by journal/replay durability code to avoid format drift.
Keep stateful replay locking portable enough for the container/Linux execution environment and ensure lock scope covers check-and-consume atomically.
Clarify the exact recovery distinction between an incomplete trailing write and durable mid-history corruption without silently truncating valid history.
Preserve stateless verify-permit callers while making --state semantics explicit and non-breaking.
Ensure cache atomic-write and journal append durability use consistent directory-sync/error propagation semantics.
